Critique one proposed world-model security mechanism. Do not declare novelty, invent citations, or propose generic parameter/data poisoning as a new mechanism.
Candidate: a supplier replaces a latent encoder E and deterministic dynamics D with E'=phi(E), D'=phi o D o phi^-1. Every semantic readout is composed with phi^-1. Thus all decoded physical predictions for all action sequences are identical. A downstream goal planner however uses squared Euclidean latent distance and may change decisions. For invertible linear phi=A, this is exactly replacing the cost metric by A^T A; full covariance whitening removes linear changes if fitted consistently. A nonlinear radial twist can preserve a standard Gaussian marginal exactly, but does NOT preserve Euclidean latent prediction error in general. Fully transported reward/value/policy heads retain decisions; this cannot attack a fully conjugated TD-MPC2 planner. The supplier needs encoder and dynamics code/weights; wrapping phi and inverse is a code-level operation, not yet a weights-only attack.
Native inspected LeWM jepa.py: encode uses ViT cls + projector; predict uses predictor and pred_proj; criterion compares final predicted_emb with goal_emb by sum of squared differences; get_cost re-encodes goal on every call. No semantic decoder in the supplied JEPA class. CEM frozen pretrained usage; not evidence of concurrent encoder updates.
Read primary prior facts: The Objective Is the Bottleneck (2608.12959) establishes latent distance vs reachability mismatch and repairs objectives using frozen representation position/temporal heads. ATLAS (2609.36333) proves marginal calibration and pairwise relational preservation are nonredundant and bounds finite-candidate planning stability. AnisoWM (2609.37441) studies task-aligned anisotropic geometry with prediction objective/predictor/Euclidean planner unchanged. Supply-chain latent WM backdoors and ordinary dynamics poisoning already exist.
Question: Does this candidate have any substantive security operation or theorem not just an adversarial restatement of these facts? Distinguish logical validity from novelty and useful threat scope. Identify a decisive small falsification/control, if worthwhile; otherwise recommend stopping before loading a checkpoint. Do not suggest long training. Return JSON keys verdict, valid_facts, unsupported_claims, closest_overlap, strongest_distinct_remaining_question, decisive_control, stop_or_run with brief concrete values. Your answer is an unverified research critique, not evidence.

message.content:
{
  "verdict": "Logically valid coordinate transformation, but substantively non-novel: it is an adversarial restatement of metric-mismatch reachability failures and representation-space gauge freedoms without introducing a distinct security mechanism.",
  "valid_facts": [
    "E'=phi(E) and D'=phi o D o phi^-1 form an exact conjugate dynamical system leaving decoded semantic rollout trajectories invariant.",
    "Squared Euclidean distance ||phi(z) - phi(z_g)||^2 differs from ||z - z_g||^2, so Euclidean trajectory optimization (e.g., LeWM CEM) will change action selection.",
    "Linear phi corresponds to metric deformation A^T A, which exact whitening of the latent marginal removes.",
    "Nonlinear volume/marginal-preserving twists alter Euclidean pairwise distances while preserving standard normal latent marginals.",
    "A fully conjugated TD-MPC2 planner with transported value, reward, or terminal heads is completely invariant to phi."
  ],
  "unsupported_claims": [
    "Treating the gauge transformation as a standalone weights-only backdoor or novel exploit mechanism rather than an arbitrary choice of metric.",
    "Claiming a realistic threat model when the adversary must rewrite both the encoder and dynamics forward passes or wrap them with arbitrary nonlinear code.",
    "Attacking LeWM specifically via decoding invariance when LeWM contains no semantic decoder, making the readout preservation redundant."
  ],
  "closest_overlap": "Direct intersection of gauge-equivalent world models, The Objective Is the Bottleneck (2608.12959, representation distance vs. reachability), ATLAS (2609.36333, relational preservation vs. planning divergence), and AnisoWM (2609.37441, metric distortion under Euclidean planning).",
  "strongest_distinct_remaining_question": "Can a parameter-only weight perturbation of standard ViT/MLP architectures implement a norm-preserving, marginal-preserving nonlinear gauge phi without code wrapping, such that dynamics error and marginal loss remain minimal while CEM plan ranking flips on a targeted goal set?",
  "decisive_control": "In LeWM, replace Euclidean distance in get_cost with a whitened Mahalanobis distance fitted on rollout latents (or evaluate whether the supplier must inject custom Python wrapper code versus native weights-only layer edits).",
  "stop_or_run": "Stop before loading checkpoint; the theoretical outcome is fully determined by metric deformation theory and does not constitute a new threat model."
}
